doc.title: Chuck Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 7, 2023

title: Dave Brubeck the man
summary: Lamb describes Brubeck as kind and gentle, recalling his stories of Art Tatum-like playing, his back injury, and meeting him and Iola.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Cannonball Adderley: the sound, the man, the band

blocks.x: Same here. Of course I had the Desmond — you know being a saxophone player Paul Desmond like — oh, something about it really grabbed me and you I guess. So what can you tell us about Dave Brubeck that really struck you?

Oh the man, oh just — he was one of the most, he was one of the kindest most gentle spirit. He was like a kid in a lot of ways. And you know we’d listen to music. I remember this one day he got out you know like four or five CDs from different people. He was always getting CDs. And we’d listen to it and talk about it and analyze, and he’d be talking about you know when he went to the Pacific, you know in college when he was a young man. And he’s going, “I could play like Art Tatum, man, I had that accident. Listen to —” and — you know because his technique was his own thing and it was a lot of rhythm-based stuff which I totally related to. But he put this thing on man and it really, it sounded like Tatum. He was just burning. And then he had that accident with his — broke his back. And you know we’ve talked about that too where he just said, “Well I had facility but I had to re-learn how to do it and as I was doing that I started developing what this sound was and I got more into rhythm.” You know it changed his direction and it made him who he was all through his — you know to have an accident like that, “Ah I’m done. I’m not going to play anymore. I can’t play like I used to” or whatever. You know he taught me so much stuff.

Did you ever hear that bit about, this was near the beginning of when his career was taking off and critics were saying he can’t swing. And there’s a thing in DownBeat where he says, “Any jackass can swing.” That’s probably the nastiest word he ever said.

Yeah, right, I was going to say man. Oh God, man, yeah that was a thrill when you asked if I was apprehensive about joining the quartet, but you know I was really excited about it but within the first minute I’m going, “When can I meet your dad?” You know I was like that’s going to happen now, I’m going to get to meet him. So that was really exciting.
My God. What a powerful, quiet powerful woman. You know? That was a killer couple, man.
